name: Tommy Boy Records
ownershipStory: Silverman started Tommy Boy out of his New York apartment in 1981 with a small loan from his parents. Its first major hit, "Planet Rock," effectively launched the label and the electro genre at once, and Tommy Boy went on to release early records by Queen Latifah, De La Soul, and Naughty by Nature before changing hands through Warner Music, then returning to Silverman's ownership in 2017.
hook: A record label started in an apartment with a family loan, that ended up releasing "Planet Rock."
blurb: Tom Silverman started Tommy Boy in 1981 with a $5,000 loan from his parents. Its breakthrough was "Planet Rock" the next year, a single that crossed over to a wider audience, and the label went on to release early hip-hop by De La Soul and Queen Latifah. It shows how small independents drove early hip-hop and electro: one loan and one crossover single were enough to start a label that stayed commercially important for four decades and through several changes of owner.
